content.text:
There are **26 open PRs** on `21nCo/super-functions`, all targeting `dev`. I pulled them from GitHub using the `thyaravind` account.

## Active work (opened 13–16 Oct)
| PR | Title | State | Checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| #248 | feat(db): JSON text codecs, correct Kysely query results | Draft, mergeable | `JavaScript` failing |
| #244 | fix(mcpfn): runtime deps, preserve schema pointers | Draft, mergeable | All green |
| #241 | SFNS-16: shared versioned API operation/release contract (+17.6k lines, 61 files) | Ready, mergeable, updated today | **GitGuardian failing**: check for a leaked secret before merging |
| #240 | feat(devfn): proxy route-transition integrity (DEV-29, slice 1/4) | Ready, mergeable | All green: **can merge now** if someone approves it |

## DocsFn documentation set (all opened 26 Sep, now stale)
- **#133 Add DocsFn documentation framework** (+283k/−39k, 834 files): has merge conflicts, and Greptile and SonarCloud are failing. The per-package docs PRs below seem to depend on it: their diffs are 3–8k lines each, and neither `docsfn/` nor `scripts/docs-site` exists on `dev` yet. So #133 probably has to land first, or they need rebasing.
- **Conflicting (13 PRs):** #206 apifn, #207 authfn (approved), #209 botfn, #214 filefn, #216 langfn, #217 mailfn, #218 mcpfn, #219 mdfn, #220 memoryfn, #221 plugfn, #222 reviewfn, #224 secfn, #225 sendfn. #220 has only one check result, and #221/#222/#224/#225 have none, probably because of the conflicts.
- **Mergeable but failing checks:** #210 clifn, #212 devfn (pullfrog also failing), #213 extfn.
- **Small and approved:**
  - #215 hostfn docs (+53/−4): mergeable and approved, but has no check results. Re-run CI, then it's the easiest merge.
  - #211 datafn (approved): only SonarCloud is failing.
  - #226 uifn (approved): only `JavaScript` is failing.

## Other
- **#228** Blacksmith runner migration (bot-opened 1 Oct, 10 workflow files): mergeable, `JavaScript` failing.
- **#180** chore(botfn): remove leftover standalone-monorepo files (rhombus-agent, 14 Sep): approved but conflicting, needs a rebase.

## Patterns
- **`JavaScript` fails on 11 PRs**, including the small ones (#226, #228, #248). That's probably a problem on `dev` itself rather than in each PR, and worth checking once.
- **SonarCloud fails on every DocsFn PR.**
- **Nothing is closable outright.** The best candidates are #215, #240 and #244 (after taking it out of draft). Then decide whether to rebase the DocsFn stack onto #133 or close it.

Below is a short description of each PR, followed by the merge order I'd suggest.

## What each PR does

**Code / features**
| PR | What it does |
|---|---|
| #248 (draft) | `@superfunctions/db`: lets a JSON field be stored in a text column instead of a native JSON column. Values are serialized on write and in query filters, and parsed on read. Also fixes Kysely results: insert returns only the requested columns, and bulk update/delete report the right affected-row counts. |
| #244 (draft) | mcpfn: updates runtime dependencies and fixes JSON Schema `$ref` lookups that contain encoded characters, which were being decoded twice. Documents the supported Node versions and adds a script that installs the packed package in a throwaway project and checks it works. |
| #241 | SFNS-16: adds a new `@apifn/contracts` package. It builds a versioned list of API operations from an OpenAPI spec plus a manifest, for SDK generators, agent tools, docs and client-error reporting. It also validates that list. Nothing uses it yet; follow-up tickets SFNS-17/23/24/25 and MCP-5 will. |
| #240 | DEV-29 (part 1 of 4 of DEV-6): makes devfn proxy route changes safe when Caddy fails or is interrupted mid-reload. New routes are marked uncertain until confirmed, the previous routes are restored on failure, and routes now record which service process owns them. |
| #228 | Bot-opened: moves all GitHub Actions workflows to Blacksmith runners and swaps `actions/checkout` for `useblacksmith/checkout@v1`. |
| #180 | botfn cleanup: deletes files left over from when botfn was its own repo (a dead nested CI workflow, duplicate vitest configs, a nested lockfile, unused dependencies) and rewrites the botfn README and AGENTS.md for the current Cloudflare layout. |
| #133 | Adds the **DocsFn framework source** to the monorepo (`@docsfn/core`, `provider-fs`, `svelte`, …), +283k lines. |

**Small docs PRs (no new site)**
| PR | What it does |
|---|---|
| #215 | hostfn: new "Administration" page on the operator service and Super Console admin integration. |
| #211 | datafn: new "Administration" page on the `@datafn/admin` executor. |
| #226 | uifn: more detail on package vs. source delivery, the npm lockfile refresh steps, and the generator script behind them. |

**New DocsFn docs sites (one SvelteKit site per package)**
#206 apifn · #207 authfn (adds a Super Console page) · #209 botfn · #210 clifn · #212 devfn · #213 extfn · #214 filefn (adds an admin page) · #216 langfn (also a small `Chain.router` fix) · #217 mailfn · #218 mcpfn · #219 mdfn · #220 memoryfn · #221 plugfn (also refreshes the core README) · #222 reviewfn · #224 secfn · #225 sendfn

## What decides the order

1. **The docs sites don't need #133 to merge first.** The existing sites on `dev` already pull DocsFn from npm (`@docsfn/core@0.0.5`, etc.), so #133 can be handled on its own.
2. **Every docs-site PR carries the same shared changes:** the shared site code in `scripts/docs-site/`, about 15–30 files moving `authfn/docs` and `filefn/docs` onto that shared code, the docs deploy workflow, and `package-lock.json`. That overlap is why 13 of them conflict with each other. Once one of them lands those shared changes, each of the others gets much smaller on rebase.
3. **#228 also edits the docs deploy workflow,** so it's simpler to merge it before the docs sites than after.

## Suggested order

**Wave 1: independent, low risk**
1. **#240** devfn route integrity: green and mergeable.
2. **#215** hostfn admin docs: approved; just re-run CI.
3. **#244** mcpfn: take it out of draft once you're happy with it; checks are green.
4. **#211** datafn docs and **#226** uifn docs: both approved. Merge #226 once the `JavaScript` check is green.
5. **#248** db JSON text storage: fix the `JavaScript` failure, then take it out of draft.

**Wave 2: needs a decision first**
6. **#241** `@apifn/contracts`: first look at why GitGuardian flagged it (possibly a test fixture that looks like a secret). Merge it before #206 (apifn docs), since both touch `apifn/`.
7. **#228** Blacksmith runners: decide whether you want it. If yes, merge it now so the docs PRs only need one rebase.
8. **#180** botfn cleanup: rebase and merge (it's approved). It should land before #209 (botfn docs) because both edit the botfn README and docs.

**Wave 3: docs sites, merged one after another**
9. Land the shared changes once. The cleanest option is a single new PR with just `scripts/docs-site`, the authfn/filefn migration and the deploy workflow, built from whichever docs PR has the newest copy (#213 was updated most recently, on 8 Oct). The alternative is to use **#207 authfn** (approved, and it has the most shared files) as the PR that brings them in.
10. Then **#214 filefn**, then the three that currently merge cleanly (**#210 clifn, #212 devfn, #213 extfn**), then rebase the rest one at a time. Do **#206** after #241 and **#209** after #180. The remaining ones (#216–#225) can go in any order.

**Last: #133 DocsFn framework.** Nothing depends on it. At 834 files and 283k lines it can't realistically be reviewed as one PR, so I'd split it into the core framework, the adapters, and the doc migrations before merging.

A caveat on Wave 3: GitHub's file list cuts off at 100 files, so for #210, #212, #213 and #219 I couldn't confirm they include `scripts/docs-site`. Their descriptions say they do.

---
title: Administration and operator service
description: Bind scoped HostFn deployment operations to a host-owned control plane.
---

The HostFn CLI deploys an application from a developer or CI machine. The separate `hostfn/operator` entry point and `@hostfn/admin` package let a host application expose deployment administration through Super Console. The capability is a contract; it does not provision a control plane by itself.

## What the host supplies

`HostFnOperatorService` takes a `HostFnOperatorStore` and a `HostFnDeploymentExecutor`. The store owns targets, deployments, domains, and variable metadata. `putVariable(variable, secretValue)` also receives the plaintext secret before the executor runs, and the memory store may retain it. Production stores must protect retained values at rest, restrict access, and avoid logging them—or deliberately avoid persisting the value while preserving the metadata required by the store contract. The executor performs external deploy, cancel, rollback, restart, domain, and variable effects. `MemoryHostFnOperatorStore` is a reference store for development and single-process installations; use a durable implementation for a production control plane.

Every operator record carries an `installationId`, `workspaceId`, `projectId`, and `environmentId` scope. The host must derive the active scope from the authenticated admin context and enforce authorization before invoking the adapter. Domain attachment uses an immutable identity and a reclaimable work lease so retries do not attach the same hostname to a different target. The external executor must be idempotent for retries with the same domain ID.

## Capability resources and actions

| Resource | Reads | Actions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Targets | List and get | Restart |
| Deployments | List and get | Deploy, cancel, rollback |
| Domains | List | Attach, detach |
| Variables | List keys | Set, delete |

Variable values are never returned by the list operation. Target server addresses are marked sensitive in the capability. Read and write operations have separate permissions. Destructive actions, including variable deletion, require MFA confirmation; variable setting requires recent authentication; deploy and domain attach require explicit confirmation for their external effects. These are declared confirmation requirements: the host must supply a confirmation service whose verifier validates the requested method and `maxAgeSeconds` freshness. The dispatcher only checks the verifier’s boolean decision; a permissive verifier does not enforce MFA or recent authentication. All writes require audit evidence through the shared admin dispatcher.

## Binding the adapter

Create an operator service with your store and executor, then pass it to `createHostFnOperatorAdminService` and `createHostFnAdminAdapter` from `@hostfn/admin`. The host must connect the adapter to its authenticated Super Console dispatcher and supply the active environment scope. The [operator source](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/hostfn/cli/src/operator.ts) and [admin capability](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/hostfn/admin/src/index.ts) define the exact interfaces and operation IDs.

Use the complete [SuperConsoleOptions and service interfaces](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/superconsole/src/lib/server/types.ts) for the binding: register the adapter in `adapters`, include `hostfn` in `enabledModules`, and implement the operator-auth provider's `authenticate` and `authorizeScope` methods as well as the mutation hook below. Keep the bundled console's default `/api/admin/v1` base path. Supply `openApiSecuritySchemes` with both `operatorSession` and `operatorApiKey` describing your authentication provider.

Every HostFn write is declared idempotent. Supply a durable store implementing the complete [AdminIdempotencyStore interface](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/packages/admin/src/idempotency.ts): `begin`, `complete`, `release`, `finalizeAudit`, `prepareCompensation`, `claimCompensation`, and `releaseCompensation`. The initial Super Console presence check inspects only the first three methods; the dispatcher constructor also requires the terminal-audit reconciliation and compensation hooks, even before an operation uses them. Implement their atomic, claim-fenced transitions and retry semantics as specified in the interface; no-op hooks do not satisfy the production contract.

Pass an idempotency key with each write request. A standalone dispatcher returns `dependency_unavailable` without a store and `precondition_failed` without a key; `createSuperConsole` rejects a missing store at startup. The operator store's domain lease protects one domain workflow but does not replace dispatcher idempotency across all mutations.

Supply a durable [AdminAuditSink](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/packages/admin/src/audit.ts) with `write` and `idempotentById: true`. The dispatcher rejects a sink without this capability marker at construction. Writes must be durable and first-write-wins by event ID, including retries after a lost acknowledgement; setting the marker alone does not provide those guarantees. Configure this sink alongside the confirmation service and authorization policies before exposing operations.

When binding through `createSuperConsole`, the operator-auth provider must implement `auth.authorizeMutation({ principal, request })`. Startup rejects the configuration without this hook because HostFn exposes mutations. The hook must reject unauthorized mutation requests; an `AdminPolicyEvaluator` does not replace this operator-auth check. Supply `shellPolicy.authorize` for console-surface access as well as the dispatcher's operation policy for scope and permission checks. These are separate authorization boundaries, not interchangeable services.

Also provide a `SuperConsoleConfirmationService`, not only a verifier. It must implement `issue`, `prepareActivation`, `cancelActivation`, `activate`, `revoke`, and `verify`; Super Console checks these methods at startup because HostFn mutations require confirmation. A token remains unusable while staged, and activation follows durable audit preparation. The service must keep cancellation and revocation effective so a denied or abandoned token cannot later authorize a write.

This integration is distinct from the CLI deployment flow. Review [deployment locks](/docs/documentation/advanced/deployment-locks), [rollbacks](/docs/documentation/advanced/rollback), and [environment variables](/docs/documentation/environment/overview) as background on the CLI implementation. The operator service delegates these effects to `HostFnDeploymentExecutor`; it does not inherit the CLI’s remote lock files, backup-based rollback, or `.env` layout. The host must implement any corresponding concurrency, recovery, and secret-handling guarantees in its executor and control plane.

=== DEV README
# botfn monorepo

[![Tests](https://github.com/21nOrg/botfn/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/21nOrg/botfn/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/21nOrg/botfn/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/21nOrg/botfn)

Turborepo-based monorepo for bot implementations with platform-agnostic architecture.

## structure

```
.
├── bots/
│   └── discord-bot/          # Discord bot with GitHub and Linear integration
│   └── [more bots...]        # Additional bot implementations
├── packages/
│   ├── discord-core/         # Discord-specific utilities and verification
│   ├── github-integration/   # GitHub API helpers
│   ├── linear-integration/   # Linear API helpers
│   └── shared-types/         # Shared TypeScript types and Zod schemas
├── AGENTS.md                 # Architecture documentation
├── package.json              # Root workspace config
└── turbo.json                # Turborepo pipeline config
```

## getting started

### install dependencies

```bash
npm install
```

### develop a bot

```bash
cd bots/discord-bot
npm run dev
```

### build all packages

```bash
npm run build
```

## npm package boundaries

The shared-types, discord-core, github-integration and linear-integration
packages ship compiled ESM with TypeScript declarations. Their builds and tests
use package-local compiler settings and declared test dependencies; they do not
resolve sibling workspace source.

The Discord bot's minimum npm prerequisite set is:

- `@superfunctions/botfn-shared-types`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-discord-core`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-github-integration`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-linear-integration`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-persistence-service`

These five foundations have no dependencies on each other and may be released in
any order before installing or releasing `@superfunctions/botfn-discord-bot`. Slack core is
independent of the Discord closure and exports both ESM and CommonJS.

Slack request verification accepts canonical decimal Unix-second timestamps only,
checks that the value is a safe integer, and rejects requests more than 300 seconds
from the current time in either direction. It verifies the HMAC against the original
request body without consuming it; the private Slack app can then dispatch signed events.

Run `npm install --workspaces=false`, `npm run build`, `npm test` and
`npm pack --dry-run` from an isolated copy of each package to check its release
boundary. Build before packing: npm exports point at `dist`, not TypeScript source.
Use `@superfunctions/botfn-persistence-service/client` for the public persistence client;
deep imports into the package's source tree are not supported.

BotFn's npm libraries live in the controlled `@superfunctions` organization.
The npm user scope `@botfn` belongs to an unrelated account; old namespace
references and release slugs are removed, not retained as aliases.


## testing

This repository has comprehensive test coverage using Vitest:

- **119 tests** across 4 packages
- **Unit tests** for core functionality
- **Integration tests** with MSW for API mocking  
- **CI/CD** integration with GitHub Actions

Run tests:
```bash
npm test                 # Run all tests
npm run test:coverage    # With coverage report
```

See [TESTING.md](./TESTING.md) for detailed testing guidelines.

## architecture

See [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) for detailed architecture documentation.

### key principles

- **Platform-agnostic core logic**: Business logic in `core.ts` is reusable across platforms
- **Multi-platform deployment**: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers, Digital Ocean, Vercel, etc.
- **Shared packages**: Common utilities and types in workspace packages
- **Type-safe validation**: Zod schemas for runtime validation
- **Monorepo tooling**: Turborepo for efficient builds and caching

## technology stack

- **Framework**: [Hono](https://hono.dev/)
- **Validation**: [Zod](https://zod.dev/)
- **Monorepo**: [Turborepo](https://turbo.build/)
- **Runtime**: Cloudflare Workers, Node.js (adaptable)

## adding a new bot

1. Create bot directory: `mkdir -p bots/my-bot/src`
2. Follow the structure in [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)
3. Create `core.ts` with business logic
4. Create platform-specific entry points (e.g., `index.cloudflare.ts`)
5. Add workspace dependencies to `package.json`

## deployment

Each bot can be deployed independently:

### Cloudflare Workers

```bash
cd bots/discord-bot
npm run deploy
```

### other platforms

See [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) for Digital Ocean and Vercel deployment guides.

Plugins implement named callbacks on `DatafnPlugin`; there is no event subscription array. `runsOn` selects the client, server, or both. Register the object with `plugins: [plugin]` when creating the client or server.

## Hook context and arguments

```typescript
import type { DatafnHookContext, DatafnPlugin } from "@datafn/core";

export const auditPlugin: DatafnPlugin = {
  name: "audit-mutations",
  runsOn: ["server"],
  beforeMutation(ctx, mutation) {
    console.log("before mutation", ctx.env, mutation);
    return mutation;
  },
  afterMutation(ctx, mutation, result) {
    console.log("after mutation", ctx.env, mutation, result);
    // This callback observes the result; its return value is ignored by the caller.
  },
};
```

`DatafnHookContext` contains `env: "client" | "server"`, `schema: DatafnSchema`, and optional host `context`. It does not contain an event name, resource filter, or payload. The operation payload is a separate argument. Treat `context` and payloads as unknown until narrowed by application code.

  done
  [ $allok = 1 ] && break
  [ $(date +%s) -gt $deadline ] && { echo TIMEOUT; break; }
  sleep 45
done
# grace period for late review bots
sleep 150
for PR in "$@"; do $S/status.sh $PR; done
EOF

# MCP server

The authfn **MCP server** is a small Node process that wraps the docs as a set of tools. MCP-aware assistants (Claude Desktop, Cursor, custom hosts) connect to it once, then have on-demand access to:

- All doc pages, by slug or full-text search.
- The OpenAPI spec — operation lookup by id, route, or tag.
- Example apps — file listings, content reads.
- Skill packs — see [Skills](./skills).

## Install

The server is published as `@authfn/mcp`:

```bash
npm install -g @authfn/mcp
```

Or use `npx` (no install required):

```bash

# Brief: bring one DocsFn site PR onto the shared docs-site runtime in dev

You own exactly one PR in `21nCo/superfunctions` (GitHub; use `GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other` for every `gh` call). The PR adds a DocsFn/SvelteKit docs site under `<pkg>/docs`. Your job is to make it merge-ready against current `dev` and drive automated PR review to zero valid findings. **Do not merge the PR.** Report back when done.

## Context
- PR #213 (ExtFn) landed the canonical shared runtime on `dev`: `scripts/docs-site/**`, the AuthFn/FileFn sites migrated onto it, `scripts/cloudflare-docs/**` product registry, the docs deploy/routes workflows, `turbo.json` (`globalDependencies` includes `scripts/docs-site/**`).
- Every other docs PR (yours included) carries its own older, diverged copy of those shared files. They must now take **dev's** version and drop their own.
- Dev docs hosting convention (from dev's `scripts/cloudflare-docs/config.mjs`): dev host `<pkg>.21n.site` on the shared `21n.site` zone in the 21n-dev account; live host/zone is the product's own domain (keep whatever live host the PR already used, e.g. `<pkg>.com`).
- Use ExtFn (`extfn/docs`) on dev as the reference consumer: `src/lib/server/docs-site-source.ts`, `vite.config.ts` (uses `docsSiteCorePlugin`), `svelte.config.js` (`@site/docs-search` alias), `tsconfig.json` (`@site/docs-search` path), `package.json` scripts (`test`, `check:llms`, `generate:llms`), `scripts/generate-llms.mjs`, prerendered `/docs/llms.txt` + `/docs/llms-full.txt` routes.

## Steps
1. Worktree: `git -C /Volumes/Dev/n/superfunctions fetch origin dev <branch>` then `git -C /Volumes/Dev/n/superfunctions worktree add --detach /Volumes/Dev/n/sfn-wt/<pkg> origin/<branch>`. Push with `git push origin HEAD:<branch>` (never force unless you rebased; prefer merging dev into the branch).
2. Dependencies: clone the installed tree instead of a 15-minute `npm ci`: `cp -cR /Volumes/Dev/n/sfn-wt/extfn/node_modules /Volumes/Dev/n/sfn-wt/<pkg>/node_modules` (APFS clone), then after merging run `npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` and `npm rebuild esbuild` in the worktree root.
3. `git merge origin/dev`. For conflicts and for files your PR changes outside `<pkg>/docs`:
   - `scripts/docs-site/**`, `authfn/docs/**`, `filefn/docs/**`, `turbo.json`: take dev's version (`git checkout --theirs` during the merge, or `git checkout origin/dev -- <path>` afterwards) unless your PR's purpose is that site's content (only #207 owns authfn/docs content and #214 owns filefn/docs content — keep their content changes but take dev's infrastructure files).
   - `scripts/cloudflare-docs/config.mjs`, `select-products.mjs`, `.github/workflows/superfunctions-docs-cloudflare-deploy.yml`, `.github/workflows/superfunctions-docs-cloudflare-routes.yml`: take dev's version, then add **only your product** following the existing entries (registry entry with dev host `<pkg>.21n.site`, selector line, workflow tags/paths/options, live-zone id env var in the routes workflow).
   - Anything else outside `<pkg>/docs` that the PR changed: keep only if it is genuinely part of this PR's purpose (e.g. a README refresh for that package or a small source fix named in the PR description); otherwise take dev's version.
   - `package-lock.json`: take dev's, then `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` to add your site.
   After the merge, `git diff --stat origin/dev...HEAD` should show essentially only `<pkg>/docs/**`, your product's registry/workflow lines, the lockfile, and anything the PR description legitimately names.
4. Adapt `<pkg>/docs` to dev's shared runtime API (mirror `extfn/docs`). Delete site-local copies of shared logic.
5. Verify locally, all must pass:
   - `npx turbo run build --filter=<site-package>...`
   - `npm test --workspace <site-package>`
   - `(cd <pkg>/docs && npx svelte-kit sync && npx svelte-check --threshold error)`
   - `(cd <pkg>/docs && node ../../scripts/docs-site/check-built-site.mjs)` after the build
   - `node --test scripts/ci-plan.test.mjs`; regenerate LLM artifacts with the site's `generate:llms` script if content changed.
6. Commit with a plain descriptive message (what changed and why). Do not mention reviews, review bots, findings or AI tools in commit messages or PR comments. End every commit message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Push.
7. Review loop. Helper scripts in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Volumes-Dev-n-superfunctions/ec9cf707-0884-40ca-b283-dbc4d0f2a4b5/scratchpad/bin/`:
   - `threads.sh <PR>` unresolved review threads; `recent.sh <PR> <ISO-time>` bot review summaries since a time; `status.sh <PR>` checks/pending/unresolved; `resolve.sh <threadId>...`; `reply.sh <threadId> "<body>"` (reply + resolve).
   - `waitsettle.sh <PR>` blocks until checks finish plus a grace period (run it in the background and wait for completion).
   For every unresolved thread and every finding in bot summaries: verify against the code. Fix valid ones (small, scoped, with tests where it is code); reply briefly with the concrete reason and resolve for invalid/out-of-scope ones; resolve threads your changes fixed. Then push and wait for the next round. Repeat until a full round produces no new valid findings, all threads are resolved, and CI is green except checks that are failing on dev itself (SonarCloud quality gate on large docs PRs is informational; note it). CodeRabbit may be rate limited; that is fine.
8. Leave the worktree in place. Report: PR number, final head SHA, what you changed (bullets), findings fixed vs rejected (with one-line reasons for rejections), CI state, anything you could not resolve.

Stay inside your PR. Do not touch other PRs' branches, do not merge, do not delete branches.
